ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: For trapezoid QRST, M and P are midpoints of the legs. If PM = 2x, QR = 3x, and TS = 10, find PM.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is trapezoid QRST, QR is the upper base, TS is the lower base, and the two are parallel; P is on the left leg QT, M is on the right leg RS, and PM connects the midpoints of the two legs and is parallel to the two bases. Reasoning: Because M and P are the midpoints of the two legs of the trapezoid, PM is the midline of the trapezoid. By the trapezoid midline theorem, PM = (QR + TS) / 2. Substituting PM = 2x, QR = 3x, TS = 10, we get 2x = (3x + 10) / 2. Multiply both sides by 2: 4x = 3x + 10, so x = 10. Thus PM = 2x = 20.

method.method_draft: Model the trapezoid with coordinates to derive the length of PM. Place the lower base TS horizontally from T = (0,0) to S = (10,0). Let the upper base QR have length 3x, so take Q = (a,h) and R = (a + 3x,h). Since P and M are midpoints of the legs QT and RS, their coordinates are P = (a/2,h/2) and M = ((a + 3x + 10)/2,h/2). Thus PM is horizontal and its length is ((a + 3x + 10)/2) - (a/2) = (3x + 10)/2. The text also gives PM = 2x, so 2x = (3x + 10)/2. Solving gives x = 10, hence PM = 20.
